Asset: RDP endpoint (TCP/3389) on VM public IP
Threat: Automated brute-force / password-spray against internet-facing RDP
Vulnerability: NSG rule "RDP" (priority 300) allows TCP/3389 from Source: Any to Destination: Any; Azure flags the rule as insecure
Justification: Likelihood is scored at the maximum because exposure is not theoretical: the Windows Security log recorded repeated Event ID 4625 (An account failed to log on) entries with a NULL SID at approximately 95-second intervals within hours of deployment, which is consistent with automated authentication attempts. Impact is 4 because a successful authentication yields an interactive session on the host but not the Azure control plane.

Threat: Credential compromise leading to full system control
Vulnerability: Password-only authentication over RDP; no MFA; azureadmin is the sole enabled local account and the only member of the Administrators group
Justification: Likelihood is 4 because the account name is predictable, the endpoint is internet-reachable, and no lockout or MFA control was observed. Impact is 5 because Administrators have complete and unrestricted access to the host, so compromise equals total loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability for the asset.

Vulnerability: Default OS configuration only; no CIS Benchmark or Microsoft security baseline applied; no Group Policy hardening; patching is unmanaged (no Azure Update Manager schedule); no VM extensions installed
Justification: Likelihood is 3 because exploitation generally requires a specific unpatched CVE rather than a guessed password, but an unmanaged patch cadence makes exposure windows open-ended. Impact is 4 because most privilege-escalation and RCE chains on this host would result in SYSTEM-level control.

Asset: Windows Security event log / audit trail
Threat: Undetected intrusion and loss of forensic evidence
Vulnerability: Logs are retained only on the local host; no diagnostic settings, no Log Analytics workspace, no Defender for Servers, no alert rules; detailed VM metrics not configured
Justification: Likelihood is 4 because malicious activity is already present in the log (4625 audit failures) and nothing is currently configured to surface it to anyone. Impact is 3 because the absence of detection does not by itself cause loss, but it extends dwell time and destroys evidence if the host is rebuilt or the log rolls over.

Asset: Azure subscription and GRC-Lab resource group
Threat: Privilege misuse or unauthorized configuration change on the management plane
Vulnerability: Single identity holds standing high-privilege access; no RBAC role separation; no Privileged Identity Management; no resource locks; no Activity Log alerts
Justification: Likelihood is 2 because the management plane is protected by the identity provider rather than by an exposed port, and the lab has a single trusted operator. Impact is 5 because control-plane compromise allows deletion, exfiltration via snapshot, or extension-based code execution across every resource in the subscription.

Threat: Lateral movement following initial host compromise
Vulnerability: NSG is bound to the network interface only. The portal reports "Impacts 0 subnets, 1 network interface" and effective security rules count is 0; there is no subnet-level NSG and no Application Security Groups
Justification: Likelihood is 2 because the lab currently holds a single workload, so there is little to move laterally toward. Impact is 4 because the NIC-only design removes a defence-in-depth layer and would not contain an attacker if additional hosts were added to the same subnet.

Asset: Outbound network path from the VM
Threat: Command-and-control beaconing or data exfiltration after compromise
Vulnerability: Default rule AllowInternetOutBound (priority 65001) permits all outbound traffic to the internet; no egress filtering, no Azure Firewall, no NSG flow logs
Justification: Likelihood is 2 because this risk is only realised after a successful initial compromise. Impact is 4 because unrestricted egress means an attacker who lands on the host can establish C2 and move data out without hitting a single control.

Threat: Ransomware, destructive attack, or accidental deletion with no recovery point
Vulnerability: Backup + disaster recovery not configured; no Recovery Services vault; no snapshots; no resource lock; auto-shutdown not enabled
Justification: Likelihood is 2 in a lab with no production data. Impact is 4 because with no recovery point the only response to a destructive event is a full rebuild, and any state on the host is permanently lost.

Threat: Offline disk access or boot-level tampering
Vulnerability: Encryption at host is Disabled and Azure Disk Encryption is Not enabled; Trusted Launch is on with Secure Boot and vTPM enabled, but integrity monitoring (guest attestation) is Disabled
Justification: Likelihood is 1 because Azure managed disks are already encrypted at rest by default using platform-managed keys, and Secure Boot with vTPM is active. Impact is 3 and the residual gap is the absence of customer-managed key control and the loss of attestation alerting rather than plaintext data at rest. Retained in the register as an accepted risk for lab scope.
